memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do the same if you find their donkey or cloak or anything else they have lost. Do not ignore it. If you see your fellow Israelite's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not ignore it. Help the owner get it to its feet. - Deut 22:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God widens the command. Whatever your neighbour has lost, a donkey, a cloak, anything, you are to return it. And if you see their animal collapsed on the road under a heavy load, you must stop and help lift it back to its feet. Again comes that key phrase, "do not ignore it." God repeats it because He knows how strong the pull is to avoid inconvenience.

Helping a fallen animal on the road was messy, tiring work. It would slow you down and dirty your hands. Yet God says stop and help. Love that honours God is often love that costs us something, our time, our comfort, our convenience. It is easy to love when it costs nothing; God calls us to love even when it does.

This reflects the very heart of the gospel. Jesus did not ignore us in our fallen, helpless state. He stopped, came down to where we were, and lifted us up at great cost to Himself. We love because He first loved us (1 John 4:19). When we help others at real cost to ourselves, we reflect the self-giving love of Christ. The next time helping someone would be inconvenient, remember how Jesus was willing to be inconvenienced, and far more, for you. Where is God asking you to offer costly help rather than pass by?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When has love cost you something recently?
2. Where are you tempted to avoid the inconvenience of helping?
3. How does Christ's costly love move you to serve others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for not ignoring me in my need but lifting me up at great cost. Help me love others even when it costs me something. Amen.
